name: Naturalisation (Einbürgerung)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires 5 years of lawful residence in Germany (reduced from 8 years since the June 2024 reform).
This requires German at B1 (Deutsch-Test für Zuwanderer, DTZ).
requirements.fix_path: Take the approved DTZ test at B1.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires passing the naturalisation test (17 of 33 questions correct).

requirements.blocker_text: This requires financial self-sufficiency — not relying on Bürgergeld (basic income support) except in narrow exempted circumstances.
This requires a clean criminal record and commitment to the free democratic basic order, including acknowledgment of Germany's responsibility for the Holocaust.
This requires 3 years of lawful residence, combined with at least 2 years of marriage to a German citizen.
This requires being married to a German citizen for at least 2 years.

notes: MAJOR LIVE POLICY EVENT already resolved, not pending: the 3-year fast-track (Turbo-Einbürgerung) route was ABOLISHED on 30 October 2025 — confirmed via multiple sources including VisaHQ's coverage of the government's own clarification. This dataset deliberately does NOT include a fast-track group, since it no longer exists; several third-party sites may still describe it as current, which would be a genuine stale-data catch if found during publication. A narrower DISCRETIONARY shortened naturalisation still exists for exceptional integration cases (C1 German, secured livelihood) but is NOT the same as the repealed automatic 3-year track — not encoded as a separate group here since it's discretionary rather than a predictable predicate-testable path, consistent with the schema's rule that non-predicate conditions go in notes, not as fake requirements. Dual citizenship generally permitted since June 2024 (Optionspflicht and retention-permit rules repealed) — a genuine structural match with the UK's position, unlike several other European countries (see Netherlands note in the original research dossier, which generally requires renunciation). Fee €255/adult confirmed; €51/minor naturalising with a parent. Naturalisation volumes are real and rising fast — Destatis recorded 291,955 naturalisations in 2024 (+46% YoY) and 332,500 in 2025, a fifth consecutive record year — worth surfacing as context on the route page rather than encoding as a schema field.
